brief:
Haidar Abu Middain, 60, sifted through the remnants of what was once one of central Gaza's most productive olive groves, tossing aside desiccated branches from felled trees across barren ground. The site bore the marks of Israeli bulldozing operations that have stripped the landscape of its agricultural foundation.

Olive cultivation has long sustained Palestinian families across Gaza. Israeli restrictions have cut off access to remaining trees, forcing residents to salvage what little remains from the destroyed groves, according to Al-Monitor reporting.
dek: By Mahmoud Issa and Nidal al-Mughrabi GAZA/CAIRO, Oct 14 (Reuters) - Haidar Abu Middain, 60, lifts a desiccated bough of a fallen olive tree and tosses it aside in the barren dirt of what was once one of the most prosperous groves in central Gaza.
title: Israeli bulldozing leaves Gazans gleaning dead olive groves
